questions.question: In which year was Sattriya dance given the status of a classical dance form by the Sangeet Natak Akademi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sangeet Natak Akademi** officially recognized **Sattriya** as a classical dance of India on **November 15, 2000**.
 
• This formal recognition increased the number of recognized Indian classical dance forms, placing **Sattriya** alongside established traditions like **Bharatanatyam**, **Kathak**, and **Kathakali**.
 
• The dance form originated in the **15th century** in the **Sattras** (monasteries) of **Assam** as a part of the **Neo-Vaishnavite movement**.
 
• It was introduced by the great saint and polymath **Mahapurush Sankaradeva** and his disciple **Madhavadeva** to preach the **Vaishnava faith** through performing arts.
 
• Historically, the dance was performed exclusively by male monks, known as **Bhokots**, as a form of worship and ritualistic practice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sattriya Dance Characteristics**:

 
 
• The performance is based on **Ankiya Nat** (one-act plays) and centers on mythological themes related to **Lord Krishna** and **Lord Vishnu**.
 
• The dance is accompanied by musical compositions called **Borgeets** and instruments like the **Khol** (drum), **Bhortal** (cymbals), and **Flute**.
 
• Costumes are distinctly Assamese, utilizing **Pat Silk** (mulberry silk) with traditional motifs like the **Kingkhap**.
 
• It follows the principles of the **Natya Shastra**, incorporating both **Nritta** (pure dance) and **Abhinaya** (expressive dance).
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi**:
 
 
• Established in **1953**, it is India's national academy for music, dance, and drama, acting as an autonomous body under the **Ministry of Culture**.
 
• Its primary objective is the preservation and promotion of India's diverse **performing arts heritage**.
 
• The academy is headquartered at **Rabindra Bhavan** in **New Delhi**.

questions.question: Which Hindu epic narrates the story associated with Dashara?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ramayana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dashara**, also known as **Vijayadashami**, is a major Hindu festival celebrated at the end of **Navaratri** every year.
 
• The **Ramayana**, traditionally attributed to the sage **Valmiki**, is the primary scripture that narrates the life and exploits of **Lord Rama**, the prince of **Ayodhya**.
 
• The festival commemorates the day **Lord Rama** killed the ten-headed demon king **Ravana**, who had kidnapped **Sita**, Rama's wife.
 
• The victory signifies the triumph of **Dharma** (righteousness) over **Adharma** (evil) and is celebrated on the 10th day of the **Ashwin** month in the Hindu calendar.
 
• In many parts of India, large effigies of **Ravana**, **Kumbhakarna**, and **Meghnad** are burned to symbolize the destruction of evil forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahabharata**:

 
 
• An ancient Indian epic attributed to **Sage Vyasa**, centered on the struggle between two groups of cousins, the **Kauravas** and the **Pandavas**.
 
• It is the longest epic in the world and contains the **Kurukshetra War**, though some regional traditions also link the **Pandavas** returning from exile to the day of **Dashara**.
 
 
 
• **Bhagavad Gita**:
 
 
• A 700-verse Hindu scripture that is part of the **Mahabharata**, specifically the **Bhishma Parva**.
 
• It presents a dialogue between **Lord Krishna** and **Arjuna** regarding the nature of duty, soul, and **Moksha**.
 
 
 
• **Vedas**:
 
 
• The oldest layer of **Sanskrit literature**, consisting of the **Rigveda**, **Samaveda**, **Yajurveda**, and **Atharvaveda**.
 
• They are religious texts containing hymns, incantations, and rituals rather than narrative historical epics like the **Ramayana**.

questions.question: Which of the following is caused by excessive nutrients in water bodies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eutrophication**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Eutrophication** is an enrichment of water by **nutrient salts**, primarily nitrates and phosphates, which causes structural changes to the ecosystem.
 
• It is triggered by the excessive entry of **nitrogen** and **phosphorus** from sources such as **agricultural runoff** (fertilizers), **detergents**, and **untreated sewage** into lakes, rivers, and coastal waters.

questions.question: The Peninsular Plateau of India is primarily composed of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Igneous and metamorphic rocks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Peninsular Plateau** is one of the oldest and most stable landmasses of the Earth, having been formed from the breaking and drifting of the ancient **Gondwana land**.
 
• It is primarily composed of ancient **crystalline igneous** and **metamorphic rocks**, which date back to the **Pre-Cambrian** era, representing the stable **Indian Shield**.
 
• The plateau is characterized by broad and shallow valleys and rounded hills, with its foundation consisting of **Archean** gneisses and schists that have undergone extensive transformation over billions of years.
 
• The region is divided into two broad categories: the **Central Highlands** (north of the Narmada River) and the **Deccan Plateau** (south of the river), both of which share this fundamental geological composition.
 
• The rocks in this region, such as **Granite** and **Gneiss**, are highly durable and have been subjected to significant **tectonic** and **denudational** processes over geological time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Igneous Rocks**:

 
 
• These are formed by the cooling of molten **magma** or **lava**. In the plateau, **Plutonic** rocks like **Granite** are prevalent in the **Bundelkhand** and **Nilgiri** regions.
 
• **Basalt**, a volcanic igneous rock, is the primary component of the **Deccan Trap**, formed by **fissure eruptions** during the **Cretaceous** period.
 
 
 
• **Metamorphic Rocks**:
 
 
• Rocks such as **Schist**, **Gneiss**, and **Quartzite** are common here, having been transformed from sedimentary or igneous precursors under intense heat and pressure.
 
 
 
• **Sedimentary Rocks**:
 
 
• While not the primary composition, they are found in basins like the **Vindhyan** and **Cuddapah** systems, containing **Sandstone**, **Shale**, and **Limestone**.

questions.question: Which of the following queens changed her name on her inscriptions and pretended to be a man?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rudramadevi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rudramadevi** (reigned **1262−1289 CE**) was one of the most prominent rulers of the **Kakatiya dynasty**, which was centered in **Orugallu** (present-day **Warangal**, Telangana).
 
• She was the daughter of King **Ganapatideva**; as he had no male heirs, he formally designated her as his successor through the **Putrika** ceremony, treating her as a son.
 
• To establish authority in a patriarchal society and gain the support of her nobles, she assumed the male name **Rudradeva Maharaja** in her **inscriptions** and often appeared in public in male attire.
 
• She successfully defended her kingdom against the **Yadavas of Devagiri** and the **Chola** empire, proving her military prowess despite initial opposition to a female ruler.
 
• The famous **Venetian traveler Marco Polo** visited the **Kakatiya kingdom** during the later years of her reign and left detailed accounts praising her administrative skills and the prosperity of her domain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kittur Chennamma**:

 
 
• She was the **Queen of Kittur**, a princely state in **Karnataka**.
 
• She is renowned for leading an armed rebellion against the **British East India Company** in **1824** in defiance of the **Doctrine of Lapse**.
 
 
 
• **Chand Bibi**:
 
 
• She served as the **Regent of Bijapur** and later as the **Regent of Ahmednagar**.
 
• She is celebrated for her valiant defense of the **Ahmednagar Fort** against the **Mughal army** led by **Emperor Akbar's** son, Prince Murad, in the late **16th century**.
 
 
 
• **Rani Durgawati**:
 
 
• She was the ruling **Queen of Gondwana** from **1550** to **1564**, belonging to the **Chandel** dynasty.
 
• She martyred herself in battle while fighting the **Mughal forces** commanded by **Asaf Khan** to protect the autonomy of her kingdom.

questions.question: Which state government has launched the 'Mukhyamantri Maiya Samman Yojana' in August 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jharkhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Jharkhand** state government, under the leadership of Chief Minister **Hemant Soren**, officially launched the **Mukhyamantri Maiya Samman Yojana** (JMMSY) in **August 2024**.
 
• The scheme is designed to provide direct financial assistance of **1,000 rupees** per month to eligible women, totaling an annual benefit of **12,000 rupees**.
 
• It specifically targets women in the age group of **21 to 50 years**, aiming to cover approximately **48 lakh** beneficiaries across the state.
 
• To facilitate the registration process, the state government organized **special camps** at the **Panchayat** and **Ward** levels between **August 3 and August 10, 2024**.
 
• The core objective of the initiative is to enhance **women empowerment**, promote **financial independence**, and improve the overall **nutritional and health status** of women from economically weaker sections.
 
• The funds are disbursed directly into the **Aadhar-linked** bank accounts of the beneficiaries through the **Direct Benefit Transfer** (DBT) system to ensure transparency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eligibility Criteria**:

 
 
• Applicants must be **permanent residents** of **Jharkhand**.
 
• The beneficiary must possess a valid **Ration Card**, such as the **Antyodaya Anna Yojana** (AAY), **Priority Household** (PHH), or **White Ration Card**.
 
• Women whose family members are **Income Tax** payers or **regular government employees** are excluded from the scheme benefits.
 
 
 
• **Implementation Details**:
 
 
• The **Department of Women, Child Development, and Social Security** is the nodal agency responsible for the execution of the **Mukhyamantri Maiya Samman Yojana**.
 
• The scheme is considered a significant **social security** initiative in the state, aiming to bridge the gender gap in financial resource management at the household level.
 
• The government allocated substantial funds in the **state budget** to sustain the recurring monthly expenditure required for this welfare project.

questions.question: Which ministry launched the Green Hydrogen Certification Scheme of India (GHCI) in April 2025?

options.text: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of New and Renewable Energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)** is the nodal agency for the implementation of the **National Green Hydrogen Mission**, which was formally approved in **January 2023**.
 
• The **Green Hydrogen Certification Scheme of India (GHCI)** was introduced to establish a standardized framework for defining and certifying **Green Hydrogen** based on its carbon footprint.
 
• According to the notified standards, hydrogen is certified as 'Green' if its **well-to-gate** emission (including water treatment, electrolysis, and purification) does not exceed **2 kg CO2 equivalent** per kg of hydrogen.
 
• The **Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE)**, which operates under the Ministry of Power, is tasked with the **accreditation** of agencies for monitoring and verifying the production processes, while the overall scheme is governed by **MNRE**.
 
• The scheme is a critical component in achieving India's **Energy Independence** by **2047** and meeting **Net Zero** targets by **2070**, ensuring that domestic production aligns with global trade requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Green Hydrogen Mission**:

 
 
• The mission has a financial outlay of **19,744 crore** and aims for a production capacity of **5 Million Metric Tonnes (MMT)** per annum by **2030**.
 
• It intends to reduce fossil fuel imports by over **1 lakh crore** and attract investments worth **8 lakh crore**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas**:
 
 
• Responsible for the exploration, production, and distribution of **natural gas** and petroleum; it oversees the transition from **Grey Hydrogen** (fossil fuel-based) to cleaner variants in refineries.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Power**:
 
 
• Focuses on the **National Grid** and **Energy Conservation**; it facilitates the transmission of **renewable energy** required for green hydrogen production through initiatives like **Green Energy Open Access**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change**:
 
 
• Handles **Climate Action** and environmental clearances; it monitors India's **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)** under international climate treaties.

questions.question: In February 2025, who among the following has launched India's first indigenous Automated Bio Medical Waste Treatment Plant "Srijanam"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jitendra Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for **Science and Technology**, Dr. **Jitendra Singh**, officially launched **Srijanam** in **February 2025**.
 
• **Srijanam** is India's first **indigenous** and **fully automated** Bio Medical Waste Treatment Plant, developed to enhance the safety and efficiency of hospital waste management.
 
• The plant is designed to handle various categories of **biomedical waste**, utilizing advanced technologies to ensure that hazardous materials are neutralized without significant human intervention.
 
• This initiative is a critical component of the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** mission, showcasing India's growing capability in high-end **medical engineering** and **environmental technology**.
 
• The project emphasizes the **Waste-to-Wealth** mission, transforming hazardous refuse into safer byproducts while maintaining strict environmental standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Srijanam Technical Features**:

 
 
• The facility employs **IoT-integrated systems** for real-time monitoring of waste processing parameters, ensuring compliance with the **Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules**.
 
• It utilizes high-efficiency **microwave-based sterilization** or **plasma pyrolysis** techniques (depending on the specific module) to achieve 99.99% microbial disinfection.
 
• The development was spearheaded by the **Department of Biotechnology (DBT)** in collaboration with private sector partners and research institutions like **IIT Delhi**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory and Strategic Context**:
 
 
• The launch supports the **National Health Policy** and the **Swachh Bharat Mission**, focusing on the safe disposal of infectious waste generated by the expanding healthcare infrastructure.
 
• By reducing reliance on imported waste treatment machinery, **Srijanam** helps lower the operational costs for Indian hospitals and clinics.

questions.question: As of August 2025, NASA confirmed nearly ____ exoplanets.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As of **August 2025**, the official **NASA Exoplanet Archive** confirmed that the number of discovered alien worlds outside our solar system has surpassed the **6,000** mark.
 
• This milestone follows the previous record of **5,000 confirmed exoplanets**, which was officially reached in **March 2022**, indicating a consistent discovery rate of several hundred planets per year.
 
• The primary driver for these discoveries is the **Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS)** mission, which has identified thousands of **TESS Objects of Interest (TOIs)** that were later validated as confirmed planets.
 
• A significant portion of these confirmations results from the legacy data of the **Kepler Space Telescope** and the **K2** mission, processed using advanced **Machine Learning** and **Artificial Intelligence** algorithms to distinguish real planets from stellar noise.
 
• Confirmation of an exoplanet typically requires detection by at least two different methods or multiple observations by independent telescopes to verify its **orbital period** and **mass**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NASA Missions and Facilities**:

 
 
• **James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)**: Launched in late **2021**, it focuses on the atmospheric characterization of these **6,000** worlds, searching for biosignatures like **methane** and **water vapor**.
 
• **Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope**: Expected to launch by **2027**, it will use **Gravitational Microlensing** to find thousands more planets in the **Milky Way**.
 
 
 
• **Detection Methodologies**:
 
 
• **Transit Method**: Measures the dimming of a star; responsible for over 75 percent of all confirmed exoplanets.
 
• **Radial Velocity**: Detects the gravitational tug a planet exerts on its host star, causing a detectable **Doppler shift**.
 
 
 
• **Planet Classifications**:
 
 
• **Super-Earths**: Planets larger than Earth but smaller than **Neptune**; they are the most common type of planet found in the current catalog.
 
• **Goldilocks Zone**: The region around a star where conditions are favorable for **liquid water**, a key focus for researchers studying the latest discoveries.

questions.question: Chandrayaan-1 mission was concluded after the communication with the spacecraft was lost in _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2009**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chandrayaan-1** was India's inaugural lunar exploration mission, launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** to study the lunar surface.
 
• The spacecraft was launched on **October 22, 2008**, from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC)** at **Sriharikota**, Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The probe was launched using the **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV-C11)** and carried eleven scientific instruments intended for chemical, mineralogical, and photo-geologic mapping of the Moon.
 
• Communication with the **Chandrayaan-1** spacecraft was unexpectedly lost at **01:30 IST** on **August 29, 2009**, after the probe had completed over **3,400 orbits** around the Moon.
 
• Following the loss of radio signals, the mission was officially declared concluded by **ISRO** on **August 30, 2009**, after approximately **312 days** in operation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scientific Milestones**:

 
 
• The mission's most significant achievement was the definitive discovery of **water molecules (H₂O)** and **hydroxyl (OH)** on the lunar surface.
 
• This discovery was confirmed by the **Moon Mineralogy Mapper (M3)**, an imaging spectrometer provided by **NASA**.
 
• The **Moon Impact Probe (MIP)**, an Indian-built instrument, successfully separated from the orbiter and struck the lunar surface near the **Shackleton Crater** on **November 14, 2008**.
 
 
 
• **Post-Mission Developments**:
 
 
• In **March 2017**, **NASA** scientists successfully relocated the derelict **Chandrayaan-1** spacecraft in a polar orbit approximately **200 kilometers** above the lunar surface using ground-based radar.
 
• The mission paved the way for subsequent lunar explorations, including **Chandrayaan-2** in **2019** and the successful soft landing of **Chandrayaan-3** in **August 2023**.

questions.question: In February 2025, 5G Lab developed by C-DOT was inaugurated at the ____ University.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gauhati**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **February 2025**, a state-of-the-art **5G Lab** was inaugurated at **Gauhati University** in Assam, marking a significant milestone for the **telecommunication infrastructure** in Northeast India.
 
• The laboratory was developed by the **Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT)**, which is the premier **Research and Development (R&D)** organization under the **Department of Telecommunications (DoT)**, Ministry of Communications, Government of India.
 
• This initiative is part of a broader national strategy to establish **100 5G labs** across various academic institutions to foster innovation and develop indigenous **5G use-cases**.
 
• The primary objective of the lab is to provide students, researchers, and startups with a platform to test and develop **high-speed communication** solutions, specifically targeting regional challenges in sectors like **healthcare, agriculture, and disaster management**.
 
• By integrating this technology into the academic curriculum, the university aims to enhance **skill development** and prepare the workforce for the evolving **6G** and **Internet of Things (IoT)** landscape.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT):**

 
 
• Established in **August 1984**, C-DOT has been instrumental in the indigenous design and development of digital exchanges and rural communication systems.
 
• It currently focuses on advanced technologies such as **Quantum Key Distribution (QKD)**, **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**, and **Indigenous 5G Core**.
 
 
 
• **Gauhati University:**
 
 
• Located in **Jalukbari, Guwahati**, it was established in **1948** and is the oldest university in North East India.
 
• It serves as a critical academic hub, supporting over **300 affiliated colleges** and driving technological literacy in the state of **Assam**.
 
 
 
• **Digital Transformation in Northeast:**
 
 
• The inauguration of such labs is a core component of the **'Digital North East Vision'**, aimed at bridging the **digital divide** and promoting **Atmanirbhar Bharat** in the telecom sector.
 
• The facility is expected to boost local entrepreneurship by providing **end-to-end 5G testbeds** for testing network software and hardware.

questions.question: S-400 missile defence system has been made by which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Russia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **S-400 Triumf**, previously known as the **S-300 PMU-3**, is a mobile, surface-to-air missile (**SAM**) system designed by the **Almaz Central Design Bureau** of **Russia**.
 
• It was developed in the **1990s** as an upgrade to the **S-300** family and officially entered service with the **Russian Armed Forces** in **April 2007**.
 
• The system is designed to provide high-altitude air defense against a variety of aerial threats, including **strategic bombers**, **electronic warfare aircraft**, **cruise missiles**, and **ballistic missiles**.
 
• It is capable of tracking up to **100 targets** simultaneously and can engage up to **36 targets** at a time using four different missile types with ranges between **40 km** and **400 km**.
 
• The **S-400** is considered one of the most dangerous operationally deployed modern long-range **SAM** systems in the world, surpassing the capabilities of many Western counterparts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geopolitical Impact:**

 
 
• **India** signed a **5.43 billion dollar** deal with **Russia** in **October 2018** to acquire five regiments of the **S-400** system to bolster its air defense against regional threats.
 
• **China** was the first foreign buyer of the **S-400**, signing the agreement in **2014** and receiving its first deliveries in **2018**.
 
• **Turkey**, despite being a **NATO** member, procured the system, which led to significant diplomatic tension and its subsequent expulsion from the **USA-led F-35** fighter jet program.
 
 
 
• **Competitor Technologies:**
 
 
• The **USA** utilizes the **Patriot (MIM-104)** and the **Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD)** systems for similar long-range defense purposes.
 
• **Germany** contributes to European air defense through the **IRIS-T SLM** and the **Medium Extended Air Defense System (MEADS)** project.
 
• **China** has developed its own indigenous long-range systems like the **HQ-9**, which incorporates elements from both **Russian** and Western technology.

questions.question: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation was established in ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shanghai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)** is a permanent intergovernmental international organization that was formally established on **June 15, 2001**.
 
• The founding ceremony took place in **Shanghai, China**, where the leaders of **China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan** signed the **Declaration of Shanghai Cooperation Organisation**.
 
• The organization emerged from the **Shanghai Five** mechanism, which was originally created in **1996** to ensure **regional security** and resolve border disputes between **China** and the former **Soviet republics**.
 
• The **SCO Charter** was subsequently signed during the **Saint Petersburg Summit** in **June 2002** and entered into full legal force in **September 2003**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Organizational Structure and Membership**:

 
 
• While established in **Shanghai**, the permanent **Secretariat** of the SCO is located in **Beijing, China**.
 
• The **Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS)**, which focuses on combating the 'three evils' of **terrorism, separatism, and extremism**, is headquartered in **Tashkent, Uzbekistan**.
 
• **India** and **Pakistan** officially joined the organization as full members during the **Astana Summit** in **June 2017**.
 
• Recent expansions include **Iran**, which became a full member in **2023**, and **Belarus**, which joined in **July 2024**.
 
• The official working languages used within the organization are **Chinese** and **Russian**.

questions.question: 2012 summer Olympic Games were held in which of the following cities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**London**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **2012 Summer Olympic Games**, officially known as the **Games of the XXX Olympiad**, were held in **London**, **United Kingdom**, from **July 27 to August 12, 2012**.
 
• With this edition, **London** became the **first city** in history to host the modern Olympic Games **three times**, having previously hosted them in **1908** and **1948**.
 
• The majority of the events took place in the purpose-built **Olympic Park** in **Stratford**, **East London**, which included the **Olympic Stadium**, the **Aquatics Centre**, and the **London Velopark**.
 
• The games saw the participation of **204 National Olympic Committees** and featured the debut of **women's boxing**, ensuring that women competed in every sport on the Olympic program for the first time.
 
• The official motto of the **London 2012** games was **'Inspire a Generation'**, aimed at creating a lasting sporting legacy worldwide.
 
• Notable milestones included **Michael Phelps** becoming the most decorated Olympian of all time and **Usain Bolt** winning gold in the **100m**, **200m**, and **4×100m relay**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paris**:

 
 
• The city hosted the **Summer Olympics** in **1900** and **1924**, and was the host for the **2024 Olympic Games**. It was the runner-up in the bidding process for the 2012 edition.
 
 
 
• **Sydney**:
 
 
• This **Australian** city hosted the **2000 Summer Olympics**, which were widely acclaimed for their organization and the significant role of **volunteerism**.
 
 
 
• **Beijing**:
 
 
• The capital of **China** hosted the **2008 Summer Olympics**. By hosting the **2022 Winter Olympics**, it became the first city to host both the Summer and Winter editions of the games.
 
 
 
• **India's Achievement in 2012**:
 
 
• India won a total of **six medals** in London, its best tally until the 2020 Tokyo Games. Medallists included **Sushil Kumar** (Silver), **Vijay Kumar** (Silver), **Saina Nehwal** (Bronze), **Mary Kom** (Bronze), **Gagan Narang** (Bronze), and **Yogeshwar Dutt** (Bronze).

questions.question: Which of the following track and field events is NOT conducted outside the stadium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3000 m steeplechase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **3000 m steeplechase** is a specialized **obstacle race** in athletics that is conducted exclusively on a **400-meter synthetic track** inside a **stadium**.
 
• It is categorized as a track event because it requires permanent infrastructure, specifically a **water jump pit** that is typically built into the **inner or outer curve** of the track.
 
• During the race, athletes must clear a total of **28 fixed barriers** and **7 water jumps**; the height of the hurdles is **0.914 meters** for men and **0.762 meters** for women.
 
• Standardization of the track surface is crucial for the **3000 m steeplechase** to ensure uniform safety and timing, distinguishing it from variable **road surfaces** used for outside events.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marathon**:

 
 
• This is a long-distance **road race** with an official distance of **42.195 kilometers** (26.2 miles).
 
• It is held on **public roads** and **urban streets**, often starting and finishing in different locations, although many major championships finish inside a stadium for ceremonial purposes.
 
 
 
• **Race Walking (20 km and 50 km)**:
 
 
• Both the **20 km walking** and **50 km walking** events are classified as **road events** by **World Athletics**.
 
• These competitions take place on **road circuits**, usually consisting of **1 km or 2 km loops** on flat terrain outside the main stadium arena.
 
• The **50 km race walk** was a long-standing Olympic event for men until it was removed after the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics** to maintain gender balance and modernize the athletic program.
 
• In these events, athletes must maintain **visible contact** with the ground at all times to avoid disqualification by judges stationed along the course.

questions.question: 'Hurkiya Baul', a traditional form of folk song belongs to which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hurkiya Baul** is a traditional folk song and dance form native to the **Kumaon region** of **Uttarakhand**.
 
• The name is derived from the **Hurka**, a small percussion instrument similar to a **Damaru**, which is played by the lead singer while performing.
 
• This folk form is intrinsically linked to agricultural activities, specifically performed during the collective transplantation of **paddy** and **maize** in the terraced fields of the **Himalayan** foothills.
 
• The performance serves as a narrative medium where the lead singer, the **Hurkiya**, recites heroic ballads known as **Gathas**, which detail the valor of legendary kings and local folk heroes.
 
• It acts as a source of motivation and entertainment for the farmers, helping them synchronize their rhythmic physical labor with the musical beats of the drum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bihar**

 
 
• Prominent folk songs include **Sohar**, which is sung to celebrate the birth of a child, and **Bideshiya**, which focuses on the pain of migration.
 
• The state is also known for **Chaita** and **Kajari**, which are seasonal songs related to the agricultural cycle.
 
 
 
• **West Bengal**
 
 
• Known for the **Baul** tradition, a group of mystic minstrels whose music is recognized as a **UNESCO Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity**.
 
• Other significant forms include **Bhatiali** (sung by boatmen) and **Gombhira**.
 
 
 
• **Mizoram**
 
 
• Features traditional songs like **Chailam** and **Khuallam**, which are often accompanied by the **Cheraw** (bamboo dance).
 
• These are typically performed during the **Chapchar Kut** festival, marking the completion of the **Jhum** operation.
